name: Délégation du Niger à l'Assemblée générale de l'ONU
detail: Voted in favor of UN General Assembly Resolution 78/230 on 22 December 2023 ('Promotion of inclusive and effective international tax cooperation at the United Nations'). Voting for an intergovernmental framework convention process does not endorse an annual net wealth tax.

name: Ali Idrissa (ROTAB / PCQVP Niger)
detail: Prominent civil society leader and coordinator of the Réseau des Organisations pour la Transparence et l'Analyse Budgétaire (ROTAB) and Publish What You Pay Niger. Led the 2018 anti-Finance Law protests; campaigned for fair taxation and transparency of multinational mining concessions (Areva/Orano uranium) and against regressive utility/consumption taxes on the poor, but did not propose an annual tax on the stock of net wealth.

name: Moussa Tchangari (Alternative Espaces Citoyens)
detail: Secretary General of Alternative Espaces Citoyens (AEC). Critiqued government fiscal policy and regressive measures in successive finance laws (notably 2018), advocating for public service funding and social justice while opposing regressive consumer taxes, without proposing an annual net wealth tax.

name: Conseil National pour la Sauvegarde de la Patrie (Fonds de Solidarité pour la Sauvegarde de la Patrie - FSSP)
detail: Enacted Ordonnance n° 2023-13 establishing the FSSP, expanded in 2024–2025; financed by a 1% mandatory deduction on monthly net salaries, 1–2% corporate turnover levies on strategic enterprises, and luxury import duties. These are salary, turnover, and import levies, not an annual tax on the stock of net wealth.

name: Gouvernement de la République du Niger (Dénonciation de la convention fiscale bilatérale franco-nigérienne)
detail: On 5 December 2023, the transitional government of Niger (jointly with Mali) denounced the 1965/1972 bilateral double-taxation convention with France (effective 2024), asserting sovereign taxing rights over corporate services and cross-border royalties. Terminating a bilateral tax treaty is not an internal net wealth tax.

name: Confédération Démocratique des Travailleurs du Niger (CDTN)
detail: Major trade union confederation led by Secrétaire Général Idrissa Djibrilla. Addressed finance law impacts, demanding downward revision of the salary tax (ITS) to protect worker purchasing power, opposing mobile money transaction levies, and defending VAT exemptions on staples; did not advocate an annual net wealth tax.

name: PNDS-Tarayya (Mohamed Bazoum / Mahamadou Issoufou)
detail: Historic ruling party and former heads of state; their fiscal programs emphasized public infrastructure, natural resource governance, and land tax modernizations (Taxe Foncière Unique - TFU on real estate), but did not propose or endorse an annual net wealth tax.

name: Hama Amadou
detail: Former Prime Minister of Niger (1995–1996, 2000–2007) and leader of the opposition party MODEN/FA Lumana Africa. Deceased on 23 October 2024 in Niamey; also never proposed an annual net wealth tax.

name: Association Islamique du Niger (AIN) / Conseil Islamique du Niger
detail: Islamic religious authorities and ulema routinely teach on Zakat as the third pillar of Islam (frequently described colloquially in French religious press as 'l'impôt islamique sur la fortune', levied at 2.5% above the Nissâb threshold). Religious almsgiving is not a statutory secular tax proposal.

name: Conseil Économique Social et Culturel du Niger (CESOC)
detail: Constitutional advisory body representing social and economic partners. Plenary sessions address tax compliance (civisme fiscal), certified electronic invoicing, and business investment incentives; no proposal for an annual net wealth tax has been issued.

name: Ibrahim Assane Mayaki (UN FACTI Panel / AUDA-NEPAD)
detail: Former Prime Minister of Niger and Co-Chair of the United Nations FACTI Panel (2020–2021). The FACTI Panel's final report 'Financial Integrity for Sustainable Development' advocated for international corporate tax minimums, beneficial ownership transparency, and combating illicit financial flows and offshore tax haven secrecy; it did not propose an annual tax on the stock of net wealth.

name: Oumarou Moumouni Dogari (Ville de Niamey)
detail: Mayor and President of the Municipal Council of Niamey (2021–2023). Managed local municipal revenues and municipal taxation (taxes de voirie, market fees, transport permits) to finance capital works; local municipal taxes and property service fees are excluded under Section 2.

name: Nouhou Arzika (Mouvement Patriotique pour une Citoyenneté Responsable - MPCR)
detail: President of MPCR; prominent civil society leader who led widespread protests against the 2018 finance law; campaign focused on fighting regressive indirect taxes (taxe d'habitation, utility hikes) and corporate tax exemptions rather than proposing a net wealth tax.

name: Maïkoul Zodi (Tournons la Page Niger / ROTAB)
detail: Coordinator of Tournons la Page Niger and member of ROTAB; organized demonstrations against the 2018 finance law demanding fiscal justice; focused on multinational tax exemptions (Areva, telecom) and reducing the cost of living for vulnerable citizens, with no net wealth tax proposal.

name: Moustapha Kadi Oumani (CODDAE / Collectif pour la Défense du Droit à l'Energie)
detail: Nigerien civil society advocate for consumer rights and energy access; author on extractive and energy revenues; advocated for general civic tax compliance and mining royalties rather than an annual net wealth tax.

name: Adamou Louché Ibrahim (Analyste Économique)
detail: Economic analyst writing for Niger Inter; published analyses on the 2018/2019 finance laws, public spending quality, and universal basic income; cited Piketty on regional monetary policy but did not propose a wealth tax.

name: Hassoumi Massoudou (Ministre des Finances 2016–2019)
detail: Minister of Finance who introduced the contested 2018 finance law; explicitly stated in media interviews that the government would not create new taxes or wealth levies, but would rely on existing customs and consumption taxes.

name: Dr. Ahmat Jidoud (Ministre des Finances 2021–2023)
detail: Minister of Finance under President Bazoum; championed "fiscalité de développement", digitalisation via e-SISIC, and broadening the tax base to gold and land property, without proposing an annual net wealth tax.

name: Ali Mahaman Lamine Zeine (Premier Ministre / Ministre des Finances)
detail: Prime Minister and Minister of Economy and Finance under the CNSP transitional government; focused on domestic revenue mobilization and customs enforcement following post-coup sanctions, alongside targeted cost-of-living tax exemptions (cement, fuel); no wealth tax proposal.

name: Haute Autorité du Waqf (HAW)
detail: Administrative body regulating Islamic charitable endowments (waqfs) under Loi n° 2020-008; administers tax exemptions for public-utility waqfs; religious charity and perpetual endowment mechanism rather than statutory wealth taxation.
